metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early November to determine progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Libya agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss proposing to hold the meeting on the first Tuesday of November.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have we decided on a date for the meeting in November? I was thinking... maybe the first Tuesday? It could work well for everyone, don’t you think? 

Also, I'm curious... is it common in your experience to discuss things like the appropriateness of government actions in these meetings?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I think the first Tuesday could be a good option, but... we should confirm with everyone else first. It’s important to find a date that suits all parties involved.

As for discussing government actions, in Libya, it's not really common to have those conversations openly. We often feel that our opinions do not matter in such matters. It's a sensitive topic.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand that confirming with everyone is important. I still believe the first Tuesday is a solid option. Maybe we can suggest it and see how others feel about it?

And I get what you're saying about sensitive topics. In China, people often feel they don't have a say in government actions either... Do you think there's a way to address these kinds of issues in a broader context, or is it too risky?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Yes, suggesting the first Tuesday makes sense. We can propose it and gather feedback. 

Regarding broader discussions, I think it's a bit too risky. People in Libya generally avoid topics like that because it can lead to complications. It's just not something we feel comfortable with in these environments. Better to focus on our work.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
That sounds good. I'll draft a suggestion for the first Tuesday and we can move forward from there.

I see your point about focusing on work. Still, I wonder if avoiding these discussions entirely limits our ability to address important issues. In China, people feel the same way about not having a voice. It's... frustrating, isn't it?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I understand your frustration, but in Libya, there's really no safe space for those discussions. It feels pointless to engage in them when we know our opinions won't lead to change. We have to prioritize our work and the project's success. It's just how things are.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I get that. Prioritizing the project's success is crucial. I'll focus on getting the meeting date sorted out.

But I can't help thinking that if we just keep avoiding these conversations, nothing will ever change. In China, people feel trapped in a similar way. Isn't it exhausting to think that our thoughts and opinions don’t really matter?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here. People everywhere have their own frustrations, but at the end of the day, it's all the same. We all want to get the job done. As long as we're speaking the same language, we can focus on what matters, which is the project. Let’s just stick to getting that meeting date set and see how everyone feels about it.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message:
Alright, I agree. Let's concentrate on setting that meeting date. I'll propose the first Tuesday and see what feedback we get. 

But I still think it’s important to acknowledge these feelings. It's... interesting how so many people feel their voice isn’t heard in different places. I wonder if ever having those conversations could lead to change someday.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: It’s good that you want to acknowledge feelings, but in our context, discussions like that don’t lead anywhere productive. It’s just better to focus on our tasks. Change is too complicated to expect from conversations. Let’s keep our attention on finalizing the meeting date and moving forward with the project. That's what we can control.
turns.label: Defense
